story.head: Reinhart’s favorite opponent
paras: The Panthers already played in Columbus once this season and left with a 7-3 win on Oct 13. The Panthers (9-7-2) lost 4-1 to Boston on Sunday, and the Blue Jackets (7-8-0) lost 5-2 to Buffalo on Friday. Going in, the Panthers are fifth in the Atlantic (16th in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th).

The Panthers have played better than their record (.556) says: their chances are worth about .626, and their finishing has held them back. The Blue Jackets’ record (.467) is about what their chances are worth.
This season, the Blue Jackets have been outscored 47-38, but only 28-25 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 12-7.

The Panthers are the league’s most physical team: first in forecheck pressure, first in physicality and first in rough stuff. The Blue Jackets, by contrast, keep things calm after the whistle (4th lowest). They also get their defensemen shooting (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (29th). Columbus has scored 2.53 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Panthers’ power play (3rd) could do real damage against the Jackets’ penalty kill (28th). On top of that, the Blue Jackets wait for good looks, but the Panthers settle for hopeful ones.

Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 22 A / 26 P in 18 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with a point in six straight games against Columbus. Brady Tkachuk (10 G / 10 A / 20 P in 18 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Zach Werenski (2 G / 12 A / 14 P in 15 GP) is next in line.

Akira Schmid (5-3-1 / .886 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for Florida. Columbus has two options in net: Jet Greaves (2-6-0 / .879 SV% in 8 GS) and Cam Talbot (5-2-0 / .909 SV% in 7 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Greaves got the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
